incidents.victim: Critical infrastructure operators — water utility, telecom, university, regional government (Portuguese- and Spanish-speaking countries)
incidents.vector: Exploitation of unpatched Microsoft SharePoint vulnerabilities (ToolShell class); attackers disabled endpoint security software on dozens of hosts before deploying Warlock ransomware.
incidents.impact: Organizations across Europe, Africa, and Latin America hit by double-extortion ransomware, including a water utility, telecommunications provider, university, and regional government; data exfiltrated before encryption.

incidents.vector: Path traversal zero-day in Fortinet FortiMail's Identity-Based Encryption (IBE) feature allowed unauthenticated attackers to write arbitrary files via null byte injection, achieving remote code execution.
incidents.impact: Exploitation confirmed before Fortinet's October 2 patch release; indicators of compromise published; scope of affected organizations not yet disclosed.

incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — ATM jackpotting (Tren de Aragua, Venezuela-based FTO)
incidents.vector: Physical installation of malware on ATM hardware by field crews, with remote activation forcing machines to dispense cash on command; proceeds laundered through cryptocurrency.
incidents.impact: Over $40.7 million stolen from U.S. banks across 1,500+ ATM attacks as of August 2025; U.S. Treasury sanctioned 10 network members on October 1, 2026, including an FBI Ten Most Wanted fugitive.

incidents.victim: Government, defense, foreign affairs, and think-tank organizations in 8 Asian countries
incidents.vector: Spear-phishing emails with spoofed sender identities triggering a five-stage infection chain deploying the Antino Rust-compiled backdoor, with command-and-control routed through Microsoft 365 Outlook and OneDrive to evade network detection.
incidents.impact: Approximately 350 endpoints compromised across 16 institutional environments in Taiwan, India, Philippines, Cambodia, Pakistan, Thailand, Myanmar, and Syria, including defense, diplomatic, legislative, law enforcement, and civil society organizations; persistent access established for ongoing intelligence collection.

incidents.victim: Government, financial services, education, telecom, and legal organizations in North America and Europe
incidents.vector: Exploitation of two Citrix NetScaler zero-days (CVE-2026-88771 and CVE-2026-88772, both CVSS 9.5) enabling unauthenticated remote code execution; first known exploitation September 3, undetected for 3+ weeks before vendor notification.
incidents.impact: Dozens of organizations compromised across North America and Europe; 50,000+ vulnerable internet-exposed instances identified; novel tunneler malware deployed for lateral movement, credential theft, and persistent access; CISA added both CVEs to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.

incidents.victim: Dozens of organizations globally — higher education, healthcare, agriculture, government, transportation
incidents.vector: Exploitation of Oracle PeopleSoft CVE-2026-35273 at scale; group also developed URL-encoding bypass to defeat the published Mandiant WAF mitigation workaround, re-compromising organizations that had applied mitigations but not patches.
incidents.impact: Web shells deployed on dozens of systems globally with full OS access in some cases; HR, payroll, and student records systems compromised; victims facing extortion threats and potential dark-web data exposure.

incidents.victim: U.S. Defense Manpower Data Center (Pentagon DMDC)
incidents.vector: Misconfigured file-sharing server left publicly accessible without proper access controls for approximately nine months (October 2025–July 2026).
incidents.impact: Personal data of 3.1 million current and former U.S. military personnel exposed, including names, military service information, and Social Security numbers; unauthorized access confirmed during the exposure window; victim notification letters being sent.

incidents.vector: Compromise of one of three operational hot wallet layers used for customer transactions; method of initial access not yet disclosed.
incidents.impact: Over $350 million in cryptocurrency stolen, making this the largest confirmed crypto theft of 2026.

incidents.victim: Air Traffic and Navigation Services (ATNS) — South Africa
incidents.vector: Ransomware-linked malware deployed against the ATNS operational technology (OT) network providing weather services to air traffic controllers; possible insider facilitation under investigation.
incidents.impact: OT weather services disrupted; ATNS manages approximately 6% of the world's airspace across domestic and international routes; attack could have crippled air traffic operations; agency reports incident is contained.

incidents.victim: U.S. Department of Defense, Department of Homeland Security (Secret Service, HSI, OIG)
incidents.vector: Oxygen Forensics Inc., a Virginia-based digital forensics software vendor, was secretly owned and controlled by five Russian nationals; software was developed in Russia and sold to U.S. agencies under false U.S.-origin certifications while the same product was sold to Russia's FSB.
incidents.impact: U.S. military and law enforcement agencies used Russian-developed forensic analysis software for years; CEO Lee Reiber and Russian co-conspirator Oleg Davydov arrested; 57 domains seized; multiple European law enforcement agencies dropping Oxygen Forensics contracts.

incidents.vector: Exploitation of Oracle PeopleSoft CVE-2026-35273 against the FBI's job application portal (apply.fbijobs.gov).
incidents.impact: Sensitive data stolen on 5,000+ FBI officials including Social Security numbers, job titles, supervisor names, and psychiatric and medical records; FBI operating under the assumption that all employee personal data was exfiltrated; Dutch police arrested a suspected ShinyHunters member on September 16.

incidents.victim: Medyc and MyDr — Polish healthcare software platforms
incidents.vector: Exploitation of vulnerabilities in cloud-hosted healthcare record platforms; the same hacking group also breached the Fakturownia invoicing platform in a related campaign.
incidents.impact: Over 24 million patient records stolen across both platforms: 5 million from Medyc and 19 million from MyDr; records include sensitive medical and personal data; both breaches attributed to the same threat actor.

incidents.victim: Asian government entities and media organizations
incidents.vector: Chained exploitation of three zero-days delivered via spear-phishing: two Chrome JavaScript engine RCE vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-85046, CVE-2026-87491) combined with a Windows ALPC privilege escalation (CVE-2026-85880); the exploit kit was shared across multiple Chinese threat groups indicating coordinated capability development.
incidents.impact: Asian government entities and media organizations targeted with previously undocumented CLEANGULP malware; coordinated kit-sharing across Chinese groups suggests broader targeting than confirmed incidents.

incidents.vector: AI-generated voice deepfake impersonating the bank's CEO Carlo Messina, combined with spoofed text messages, convinced Fideuram's chairman to authorize wire transfers to Chinese and Hong Kong accounts.
incidents.impact: €95 million ($108 million) fraudulently transferred; Intesa Sanpaolo recovered more than half, but €36 million remains unrecovered.

incidents.vector: Social engineering: a ShinyHunters member phoned an Odido employee, impersonated a trusted party, and tricked them into authenticating to a spoofed internal portal, harvesting session credentials used to access and exfiltrate customer data.
incidents.impact: Data stolen on more than 6.2 million Dutch citizens; Dutch police are investigating and have released a recording of the attacker's voice seeking public identification of the suspect.
